title: Identify Design Principles of the AWS Cloud

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS wants you to recognize principles used to build and operate cloud workloads effectively.
sections.callout: Which Well-Architected pillar best matches the requirement in the scenario?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
sections.callout: RUN → PROTECT → RECOVER → PERFORM → SAVE → SUSTAIN

sections.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework
paragraphs: The AWS Well-Architected Framework helps organizations understand how to design and operate workloads using cloud architecture practices. It provides a structured way to evaluate architectural decisions through six pillars.
sections.callout: Are we building and operating this workload well?

sections.title: Operational Excellence
paragraphs: Operational Excellence focuses on supporting development, running workloads effectively, and continually improving processes and procedures.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: The Security pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets while supporting business requirements.

sections.title: Reliability
paragraphs: Reliability focuses on a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, including recovery when something fails.
sections.callout: KEEP IT WORKING—AND RECOVER WHEN IT BREAKS

sections.title: Performance Efficiency
paragraphs: Performance Efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements as demand and technologies change.

sections.title: Cost Optimization
paragraphs: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary expense while delivering the required business value. It does not mean choosing the cheapest option regardless of the outcome.
sections.callout: DO NOT PAY FOR WHAT YOU DO NOT NEED

sections.title: Sustainability
paragraphs: The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads.
sections.callout: DO THE WORK WITH LESS ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT

sections.title: Distinguishing the Six Pillars
paragraphs: Identify the primary concern. Another pillar may be related, but the exam asks for the best match.

table.caption: Primary concern and its Well-Architected pillar
rows: Recover from failures and continue functioning

entries.title: Operational Excellence vs. Reliability
paragraphs: Improve how systems are operated → Operational Excellence. Recover when systems fail → Reliability.

entries.title: Security vs. Reliability
paragraphs: Protection or unauthorized access → Security. Failure or recovery → Reliability.

entries.title: Reliability vs. Performance Efficiency
paragraphs: Can it continue or recover? → Reliability. Is it efficiently meeting performance requirements? → Performance Efficiency.

entries.title: Performance Efficiency vs. Cost Optimization
paragraphs: Optimize performance and resource selection → Performance Efficiency. Optimize spending → Cost Optimization.

entries.title: Cost Optimization vs. Sustainability
paragraphs: Reduce financial waste → Cost Optimization. Reduce environmental impact → Sustainability.

entries.title: Operational Excellence vs. Performance Efficiency
paragraphs: Improve operational procedures → Operational Excellence. Improve efficient use of computing resources → Performance Efficiency.
